prerequisites: Knowledge of basic mathematics concepts: algebra, geometry, differential calculus, integral calculus, differential equations, vector calculus.
Knowledge of measurement unit systems and fundamental laws of Newtonian mechanics and thermodynamics.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic notions of electromagnetism and optics based on the experimental scientific method.

Be able to tackle problems related to the topics covered, correctly setting up and solving a physical situation proposed in the form of an exercise, through the application of appropriate physical laws.
Demonstrate the ability to solve algebraically and numerically proposed problems.
Be able to provide a critical description of the physical phenomena considered, formulating the laws in a mathematically correct manner.

syllabus_topics: Electrostatic field and potential of continuous charge distributions
Series and parallel connections of capacitors
Polarization charge and its surface density
Relationship between polarization and electric field: electric susceptibility
Electric current and electric current density
Resistivity and conductivity, Ohm's law of conduction
Charging and discharging of a capacitor
Magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor: II elementary law of Laplace
Motion of charges in magnetic field
Mechanical moment on a current-carrying loop
Magnetic field produced by a current
Applications of the first law of Laplace
Magnetic field flux and Gauss's law
Flux linked with a closed line
Field of an infinite straight solenoid and a toroidal solenoid
Brief overview of the origins of the magnetic dipole
Relationship between B, H, and M
Rotating vector method and generalized Ohm's law
Electric and magnetic energy of the oscillator
Series RCL circuit: damped and forced oscillations
Derivation of electromagnetic waves from the solution of Maxwell's equations in vacuum
Energy and intensity of electromagnetic wave
Brief overview of anisotropic materials, dichroism, and polarizers
teaching_methods: Use of technological tools (moodle and/or other educational tools, software, videos, quizzes)
In person theory lectures with exercises and application examples
Laboratory activities with the performance of significant experiments for understanding theoretical models

assessment_methods.method: Ongoing written test (1 written problem in electrostatics)
Written exams during the official sessions (3 exercises/problems to do)

assessment_rules: Summative assessment is on a 30-point scale. Students must have 100% laboratory attendance (one absence can be recovered). The exam includes an ongoing written test (one problem in electrostatics), written exams during official sessions (three exercises/problems), and an oral exam. The use of all communication and interconnection devices, as well as AI tools, is strictly prohibited during exams; electronic calculators are allowed.
